nodes.summary: If every graph on $N$ vertices contains $K_s$ or has $K_t$ in its complement, then the same holds for every graph on $M \ge N$ vertices: restrict the graph to its first $N$ vertices, find $K_s$ or a complementary $K_t$ there, and include it back. Hence the set of $N$ with the Ramsey property is upward closed, and $R(s, t) > n$ as soon as the property fails on $n$ vertices.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the Ramsey property

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $s$, $t$ and $N$, the classical Ramsey property for $(s, t)$ holds at $N$ when every simple graph $G$ on $N$ vertices contains the complete graph $K_s$ as a subgraph, or its complement $\overline{G}$ contains $K_t$ as a subgraph.
nodes.title: The Ramsey property for cliques

nodes.summary: The proposition asserts that there is a real number $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which no two adjacent vertices both have degree at least $3$, the diagonal Ramsey number $R(G, G)$ is at most $Cn$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 800 on linear Ramsey numbers

nodes.summary: There is a real number $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which no two adjacent vertices both have degree at least $3$, the diagonal Ramsey number $R(G, G)$ is at most $Cn$.
nodes.title: Alon's theorem on linear Ramsey numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 3$ there is an $M$ such that for every $m \ge M$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with exactly $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, the Ramsey number $R(C_k, H)$ of the cycle $C_k$ on $k$ vertices and $H$ is at most $2m + \lfloor (k-1)/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Resolution of Erdős Problem 570

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $k \ge 3$ there is an $M$ such that for every $m \ge M$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with exactly $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, the Ramsey number $R(C_k, H)$ of the cycle $C_k$ on $k$ vertices and $H$ is at most $2m + \lfloor (k-1)/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 570 (cycle versus graph Ramsey bound)

nodes.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, the diagonal Ramsey number of $G$ is $R(G, G)$: the least $n$ such that for every simple graph $C$ on $n$ vertices, $C$ or its complement contains a copy of $G$ as a subgraph, and $0$ if there is no such $n$.
nodes.title: Diagonal Ramsey number of a graph

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $s$ and $t$ there is an $N$ such that every simple graph on $N$ vertices contains $K_s$ or has $K_t$ in its complement. Colour each pair of vertices by whether it is an edge; the finite Ramsey theorem for pairs gives a monochromatic set of size $\max(s, t)$, which contains a $K_s$ in the graph or a $K_t$ in its complement. Hence the set defining the classical Ramsey number $R(s,t)$ is…
nodes.title: Existence of Ramsey numbers for cliques

nodes.summary: Every sufficiently large $n$ has a triangle-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with which follows from Kim's bound on the independence number and $\chi(G) \ge n / \alpha(G)$. With the upper bound on $R(3,t)$ it determines the maximum chromatic number of triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices up to a constant factor: between $(1 - o(1)) \frac19 \sqrt{n/\log n}$ and $(1 + o(1)) 2\sqrt2 \sqrt{n/\log n}$.
nodes.title: Chromatic number of Kim's triangle-free graphs

nodes.summary: Every sufficiently large $n$ has a triangle-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with (natural logarithm). Kim builds $G$ by a semi-random ("nibble") block construction: in each round every edge that does not close a triangle with the edges chosen so far is added independently with probability $\theta / \sqrt n$, $\theta = (\log n)^{-2}$, and a maximal disjoint family of conflicting pairs and triples is removed.…
nodes.title: Kim's triangle-free graphs with small independence number

nodes.summary: Let $n, k$ be natural numbers with Then there is a simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that neither $G$ nor its complement contains $K_k$; equivalently, the edges of $K_n$ can be coloured red and blue with no monochromatic $K_k$.
nodes.title: Erdős's lower bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers (existence form)

nodes.summary: If the graph with edge set $\omega$ contains a copy of $K_k$, its vertex set is a $k$-set $R$ all of whose pairs belong to $\omega$; if the complement contains a copy of $K_k$, all pairs of $R$ lie outside $\omega$. This translates "contains $K_k$" into the events $\{S \subseteq \omega\}$ and $\{S \cap \omega = \emptyset\}$ of the random-subset model.
nodes.title: A copy of K_k gives a monochromatic k-set

nodes.summary: For finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $R(G, H)$ equals the infimum in $\mathbb{N}$ (where the empty set has infimum $0$) of the set of $n$ such that every simple graph $C$ on $n$ vertices contains a copy of $G$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing a copy of $H$ as a subgraph.
nodes.title: The pair Ramsey number as an infimum

nodes.summary: For finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $R(G, H)$ is the least $n$ such that every simple graph $C$ on $n$ vertices contains a copy of $G$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing a copy of $H$ as a subgraph, and $0$ if there is no such $n$.
nodes.title: Ramsey number of a pair of graphs

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $s$ and $t$, the Ramsey number $R(s, t)$ equals the infimum in $\mathbb{N}$ (where the empty set has infimum $0$) of the set of $N$ such that every simple graph on $N$ vertices contains the complete graph $K_s$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing $K_t$ as a subgraph.
nodes.title: Classical Ramsey numbers as an infimum

nodes.summary: As $t \to \infty$, the combination of Kim's lower bound and the upper bound of Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi and Shearer. This settled the order of magnitude of $R(3,t)$, open since Erdős's 1961 bound; Kim received the 1997 Fulkerson Prize for it.
nodes.title: R(3, t) has order of magnitude t² / log t

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $t$, that is, $R(3,t) \ge c(1 - o(1))\, t^2/\log t$ with $c = 1/162 = 1/(2 \cdot 9^2)$. It follows from Kim's triangle-free graphs: a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\alpha < t$ shows $R(3, t) > n$. Earlier lower bounds were of order $t^2 / (\log t)^2$ (Erdős 1961, with later simplifications and better constants by Spencer, Bollobás,…
nodes.title: Kim's lower bound for R(3, t)

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $t$, Ajtai, Komlós and Szemerédi proved $R(3,t) = O(t^2 / \log t)$, removing the $\log \log t$ factor of Graver and Yackel; Shearer reduced the constant to $1 + o(1)$ and simplified the proof.
nodes.title: Upper bound for R(3, t) (Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi, Shearer)

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $s$ and $t$, the Ramsey number $R(s, t)$ is the least $N$ such that every simple graph on $N$ vertices contains the complete graph $K_s$ as a subgraph or has a complement containing $K_t$ as a subgraph, and $0$ if there is no such $N$.
nodes.title: Classical Ramsey numbers

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. For a finite simple graph $H$, write $R(G, H)$ for the least $m$ such that every simple graph on $m$ vertices contains a copy of $G$ or has a complement containing a copy of $H$ ($0$ if there is no such $m$), and write $e(H)$ for the number of edges of $H$. Then $G$ is Ramsey size linear if there is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for every $n$ and every simple graph $H$ on $n$…
nodes.title: Ramsey size linear graphs

nodes.summary: If $\binom nk 2^{1 - \binom k2} < 1$, then $n < R(k, k)$ for the repository's classical Ramsey number `graphRamsey k k`. The least $N$ with the Ramsey property exists by the existence of Ramsey numbers, and it exceeds $n$ by Erdős's lower bound. For example $R(5, 5) > 11$.
nodes.title: Erdős's lower bound, graphRamsey form

nodes.summary: If $\binom nk 2^{1 - \binom k2} < 1$, then every $N$ such that every graph on $N$ vertices contains $K_k$ or has $K_k$ in its complement satisfies $N > n$; that is, $R(k, k) > n$. Optimising $n$ (with Stirling's formula) gives $R(k,k) > (1/(e\sqrt2) + o(1))\, k\, 2^{k/2}$ (Zhao, Fact 1.5); the notes record that improving the exponential base $\sqrt 2$ is open.
nodes.title: Erdős's lower bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers

nodes.summary: If $\binom nk 2^{1 - \binom k2} < 1$, then the Ramsey property for $(k, k)$ fails on $n$ vertices: some graph on $n$ vertices contains no $K_k$, and neither does its complement. This restates the existence form in terms of the Ramsey property for cliques. For example $\binom 64 2^{-5} = 15/32 < 1$ gives $R(4,4) > 6$, and $\binom{11}5 2^{-9} = 462/512 < 1$ gives $R(5,5) > 11$.
nodes.title: Erdős's bound: the Ramsey property fails

nodes.summary: For a set $\omega$ of pairs of vertices, the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct $i$ and $j$ are adjacent exactly when $\{i, j\} \in \omega$. Read as a red–blue colouring of the edges of $K_n$, its edges are the red ones and the edges of its complement the blue ones. With $\omega$ the random subset of pairs with $p = 1/2$ it is the uniformly random graph $G(n, 1/2)$, and with constant $p$ the…
nodes.title: Graph with a given set of pairs as edges

nodes.summary: The two-element subsets $\{i, j\}$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$: the $\binom n2$ possible edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is the same thing as a set of pairs, and a uniformly random graph is a random subset of the pairs, each kept with probability $1/2$.
nodes.title: Pairs of vertices

nodes.summary: For a set $R$ of vertices, the pairs $\{i, j\} \subseteq R$; there are $\binom{|R|}{2}$ of them. $R$ is a clique of the graph with edge set $\omega$ when all of them are in $\omega$, and an independent set when none is.
nodes.title: Pairs inside a vertex set

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every real number $C$, for all sufficiently large natural numbers $n$, every connected graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $Cn$ edges has $R(K_3, G) = 2n - 1$. Equivalently, there is a real number $C$ such that for infinitely many $n$ some connected graph $G$ on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $Cn$ edges has $R(K_3, G) \ne 2n - 1$. Here $R(K_3, G)$ is the Ramsey…
nodes.title: No superlinear threshold for triangle-good graphs (Erdős Problem 1182)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every real number $C$, for all sufficiently large natural numbers $n$, every connected graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $Cn$ edges has $R(K_3, G) = 2n - 1$. Here $R(K_3, G)$ is the Ramsey number of the pair: the least $N$ such that every graph on $N$ vertices contains a triangle or has a complement containing a copy of $G$.
